blocks.text: Practice long questions for the whole of Unit 9 (Inverse Trigonometric (TOC: 'Inverse Trigonometric Functions and Their Graphs')), in the shape of a Board Section-II question part: each carries 5 marks (a longer problem, a proof or a derivation). Each one is solved in full, step by step.

blocks.prompt: 1 Prove that (i) \(\cos^{-1}(-x) = \pi - \cos^{-1} x\) (ii) \(\sin^{-1}(-x) = -\sin^{-1} x\), for \(-1 \le x \le 1\). Verify both for \(x = \frac{1}{2}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Name the angle, use cos(pi - t) = -cos t and sin(-t) = -sin t, and check that the new angle is in the principal range.

book_ref.quote: A pattern you can see in the table

steps: From \(0 \le \theta \le \pi\): \(0 \le \pi - \theta \le \pi\), the range of \(\cos^{-1}\); so \(\cos^{-1}(-x) = \pi - \theta = \pi - \cos^{-1} x\)

blocks.prompt: 2 Find the principal value of (i) \(\sin^{-1}\left(\sin\frac{5\pi}{6}\right)\) (ii) \(\cos^{-1}\left(\cos\left(-\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)\right)\) (iii) \(\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\frac{7\pi}{6}\right)\) (iv) \(\sec^{-1}\left(\sec\left(-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\right)\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Work out the inner value first, then pick the one angle with that value inside the principal range (the answer is not simply the given angle).

book_ref.quote: How to find a principal value (the method of Example 1)

blocks.prompt: 3 Prove that \(\cot^{-1} x = \pi + \tan^{-1}\frac{1}{x}\) for \(x < 0\). Verify it for \(x = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: For negative \(x\) the angle \(\cot^{-1} x\) is obtuse, outside the range of \(\tan^{-1}\); move it into that range by subtracting \(\pi\) (tangent has period \(\pi\)).

book_ref.quote: For negative \(x\) the correct relation is

steps: Let \(y = \cot^{-1} x\) with \(x < 0\); then \(\cot y = x\) and \(y \in \left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right)\)
\(y - \pi\) lies in the range of \(\tan^{-1}\), so \(y - \pi = \tan^{-1}\frac{1}{x}\), i.e. \(\cot^{-1} x = \pi + \tan^{-1}\frac{1}{x}\)
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(\cot^{-1} x = \pi + \tan^{-1}\frac{1}{x}\) for \(x < 0\); for \(x = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) both sides are \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\).

blocks.prompt: 4 Find the domain of (i) \(f(x) = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{x - 1}{2}\right) + \sec^{-1}(x + 1)\) (ii) \(g(x) = \cos^{-1}(x^{2} - 1)\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Each inverse function needs its input in its own domain; for a sum both conditions must hold, so take the common part.

book_ref.quote: an inverse trigonometric function only accepts inputs from its own domain

blocks.prompt: 5 Without using a calculator find (i) \(\sin\left(\frac{1}{2}\cos^{-1}\frac{17}{25}\right)\) (ii) \(\cos\left(\frac{1}{2}\sec^{-1}\frac{9}{7}\right)\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Name the inner angle \(\alpha\), find \(\cos\alpha\), and use the half-angle identities \(\sin\frac{\alpha}{2} = \sqrt{\frac{1 - \cos\alpha}{2}}\), \(\cos\frac{\alpha}{2} = \sqrt{\frac{1 + \cos\alpha}{2}}\) (positive roots for an acute \(\frac{\alpha}{2}\)).

book_ref.quote: which needs only \(\cos\alpha\)

blocks.prompt: 6 Prove that \(\cos(\tan^{-1} x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 + x^{2}}}\) and \(\sin(\tan^{-1} x) = \frac{x}{\sqrt{1 + x^{2}}}\) for every real \(x\). Hence find \(\cos\left(\tan^{-1}\left(-\frac{3}{4}\right)\right)\) and \(\sin\left(\tan^{-1}\left(-\frac{3}{4}\right)\right)\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Name the angle; \(1 + \tan^{2}\alpha = \sec^{2}\alpha\) gives \(\cos\alpha\), with the sign fixed by the principal range \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\).

book_ref.quote: build the point \((3, 4)\) to get \(\sin\alpha\) and \(\cos\alpha\)

blocks.prompt: 7 Derive the formula \(\sin^{-1} x + \sin^{-1} y = \sin^{-1}\left(x\sqrt{1 - y^{2}} + y\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\right)\), stating why the positive square roots are taken. Verify it for \(x = 0.3\), \(y = 0.4\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Name the two angles, find their cosines (non-negative in the principal range), expand sin(a + b), then take the inverse sine.

book_ref.quote: Since \(\alpha, \beta \in \left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\), so \(\cos\alpha, \cos\beta \ge 0\)

steps: Let \(\sin^{-1} x = \alpha \Rightarrow \sin\alpha = x\) and \(\sin^{-1} y = \beta \Rightarrow \sin\beta = y\), with \(\alpha, \beta \in \left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\)
\(\cos\alpha = \pm\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\); in \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) cosine is not negative, so \(\cos\alpha = \sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\), and similarly \(\cos\beta = \sqrt{1 - y^{2}}\)
When \(\alpha + \beta\) lies in \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) (e.g. \(x^{2} + y^{2} \le 1\)): \(\alpha + \beta = \sin^{-1}\left(x\sqrt{1 - y^{2}} + y\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\right)\)
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(\sin^{-1} x + \sin^{-1} y = \sin^{-1}\left(x\sqrt{1 - y^{2}} + y\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\right)\) (when \(\alpha + \beta \in \left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\)).

blocks.prompt: 8 Prove that \(\sin^{-1} x - \sin^{-1} y = \sin^{-1}\left(x\sqrt{1 - y^{2}} - y\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\right)\). Verify it for \(x = \frac{12}{13}\), \(y = \frac{4}{5}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Same start as formula (i), but expand sin(a - b).

book_ref.quote: (ii) Same start as (i), but use

steps: \(\cos\alpha = \sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\), \(\cos\beta = \sqrt{1 - y^{2}}\) (cosine is not negative in this interval)
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(\sin^{-1} x - \sin^{-1} y = \sin^{-1}\left(x\sqrt{1 - y^{2}} - y\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\right)\); for the given values both sides equal \(\sin^{-1}\frac{16}{65}\).

blocks.prompt: 9 Prove that \(\cos^{-1} x + \cos^{-1} y = \cos^{-1}\left(xy - \sqrt{(1 - x^{2})(1 - y^{2})}\right)\) (valid when \(x + y \ge 0\)). Verify it for \(x = y = \frac{1}{2}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Now the angles lie in \([0, \pi]\), where the sine (not the cosine) is never negative; expand \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\) with the minus sign.

book_ref.quote: Now \(\alpha, \beta \in [0, \pi]\), so

steps: In \([0, \pi]\) sine is not negative: \(\sin\alpha = \sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\), \(\sin\beta = \sqrt{1 - y^{2}}\)
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(\cos^{-1} x + \cos^{-1} y = \cos^{-1}\left(xy - \sqrt{(1 - x^{2})(1 - y^{2})}\right)\); both sides are \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\) for \(x = y = \frac{1}{2}\).

blocks.prompt: 10 Prove that \(\cos^{-1} x - \cos^{-1} y = \cos^{-1}\left(xy + \sqrt{(1 - x^{2})(1 - y^{2})}\right)\) (valid when \(x \le y\)). Verify it for \(x = 0\), \(y = \frac{1}{2}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Same start as formula (iii), but expand \(\cos(\alpha - \beta)\), which has a plus sign.

book_ref.quote: (iv) The same, with \(\cos(\alpha - \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta + \sin\alpha\sin\beta\)

steps: Let \(\cos^{-1} x = \alpha\), \(\cos^{-1} y = \beta\); \(\alpha, \beta \in [0, \pi]\), so \(\sin\alpha = \sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\), \(\sin\beta = \sqrt{1 - y^{2}}\)
If \(x \le y\), then \(\alpha \ge \beta\) (\(\cos^{-1}\) is decreasing), so \(0 \le \alpha - \beta \le \pi\), inside the range of \(\cos^{-1}\)
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(\cos^{-1} x - \cos^{-1} y = \cos^{-1}\left(xy + \sqrt{(1 - x^{2})(1 - y^{2})}\right)\); both sides are \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) for the given values.

blocks.prompt: 11 Prove that \(\tan^{-1} x + \tan^{-1} y = \tan^{-1}\frac{x + y}{1 - xy}\) (\(xy < 1\)). Deduce that \(2\tan^{-1} x = \tan^{-1}\frac{2x}{1 - x^{2}}\) for \(-1 < x < 1\), and use it to find \(2\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{2}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Name the angles, use \(\tan(\alpha + \beta) = \frac{\tan\alpha + \tan\beta}{1 - \tan\alpha\tan\beta}\), then put \(y = x\).

book_ref.quote: Next, we proceed to prove formula (v) as follows

steps: Let \(\tan^{-1} x = \alpha \Rightarrow \tan\alpha = x\) and \(\tan^{-1} y = \beta \Rightarrow \tan\beta = y\)
For \(xy < 1\), \(\alpha + \beta\) lies in \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\), so \(\alpha + \beta = \tan^{-1}\frac{x + y}{1 - xy}\)
Put \(y = x\): \(2\tan^{-1} x = \tan^{-1}\frac{2x}{1 - x^{2}}\); the condition \(x \cdot x < 1\) is \(-1 < x < 1\)

blocks.prompt: 12 Prove that \(\tan^{-1} x - \tan^{-1} y = \tan^{-1}\frac{x - y}{1 + xy}\) (\(xy > -1\)). Verify it for \(x = 1\), \(y = \frac{1}{3}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: As for formula (v), but with \(\tan(\alpha - \beta) = \frac{\tan\alpha - \tan\beta}{1 + \tan\alpha\tan\beta}\).

book_ref.quote: For (vi) take the same \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\)

blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(\tan^{-1} x - \tan^{-1} y = \tan^{-1}\frac{x - y}{1 + xy}\); here \(\tan^{-1} 1 - \tan^{-1}\frac{1}{3} = \tan^{-1}\frac{1}{2}\).

blocks.prompt: 13 Deduce \(2\sin^{-1} x = \sin^{-1}\left(2x\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\right)\) from formula (i) and \(2\cos^{-1} x = \cos^{-1}(2x^{2} - 1)\) from formula (iii). Use them to write \(2\sin^{-1}\frac{1}{3}\) and \(2\cos^{-1}\frac{1}{3}\) as single inverse functions. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Put y = x in formulas (i) and (iii); check the conditions before using the results.

book_ref.quote: The second result comes from (iii)

steps: Put \(y = x\) in (i): \(2\sin^{-1} x = \sin^{-1}\left(x\sqrt{1 - x^{2}} + x\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\right) = \sin^{-1}\left(2x\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\right)\), valid for \(|x| \le \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\)

blocks.prompt: 14 Prove that \(\cos^{-1} x = \tan^{-1}\frac{\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}}{x}\) for \(0 < x \le 1\). Hence show that \(\cos^{-1}\frac{5}{13} = \tan^{-1}\frac{12}{5}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Name the angle, find \(\sin\alpha\) (positive in \([0, \pi]\)), divide to get \(\tan\alpha\), and check that \(\alpha\) is in the range of \(\tan^{-1}\).

book_ref.quote: The same triangle idea turns any inverse function into another.

book_ref.quote: These identities can be derived by applying the fundamental trigonometric identities along with algebraic manipulation.

blocks.prompt: 20 Prove that \(\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{2} + \tan^{-1}\frac{1}{5} + \tan^{-1}\frac{1}{8} = \frac{\pi}{4}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Join two terms at a time with formula (v), checking xy < 1 each time.

book_ref.quote: They join two inverse functions into one.

blocks.prompt: 21 Prove that \(4\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{5} - \tan^{-1}\frac{1}{239} = \frac{\pi}{4}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Double twice with \(2\tan^{-1} x = \tan^{-1}\frac{2x}{1 - x^{2}}\) (each time \(|x| < 1\)), then subtract with formula (vi).

book_ref.quote: Double results: \(2\tan^{-1}x = \tan^{-1}\frac{2x}{1-x^{2}}\)

blocks.prompt: 22 Solve the equation \(\tan^{-1} 2x + \tan^{-1} 3x = \frac{\pi}{4}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Join the two angles with formula (v), take tan of both sides, solve the quadratic, then test each root in the original equation.

book_ref.quote: In equations, test every root in the original equation

steps: Test \(x = -1\): \(\tan^{-1}(-2) + \tan^{-1}(-3)\) is negative (\(= -\frac{3\pi}{4}\)), not \(\frac{\pi}{4}\); here \(xy = 6 > 1\). Rejected

blocks.prompt: 23 Solve the equation \(\tan^{-1}(x + 1) + \tan^{-1}(x - 1) = \tan^{-1}\frac{8}{31}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Join the left side with formula (v), equate the fractions, solve the quadratic and test both roots.

book_ref.quote: always substitute every root back into the original equation
